correctness.rationale: For Haar-a.e. irrational base orbit, Birkhoff applies to integrable log g_d, yielding the neutral exponent. Strict leave-one-out Jensen comparison yields all d inequalities. Two-dimensional evaluation follows from Abel-integrated logarithmic Fourier series with only odd frequencies. For large d, bounded i.i.d. sine moments, Taylor expansion through order six, exponential Hoeffding tail and AM–GM logarithmic lower bound yield the stated 1/d² coefficients and O(d^-3) remainder. Strict sign transition and inverse asymptotic then follow. The included checker validates algebraic moments and numerical special cases but does not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The integral formula and the model are credited to earlier literature. The joint theorem identifies strict dependence on ambient forcing dimension and evaluates two genuinely quantitative objects (the d=2 Apéry value and the two-term high-d expansion), from which a unique dimension threshold for fixed forcing follows. The two primary same-map PDFs were compared at the level of definitions and statements; neither asserts these conclusions. General sample-mean convex-order methods are standard and are not claimed as innovations. Full priority remains provisional against unindexed work.
residual_risks: A general exact integral formula already appears in the 2022 source, so the novelty is in quantitative comparison rather than the setup or exponent identity.
The earlier 2011 paper first introduces the same model; it is included as substantive cross-era prior work rather than omitted.
The Keller 1996 full paper was inaccessible; equivalent statements in unpublished/unindexed dynamical or trigonometric-integral literature cannot be excluded.
The transition threshold belongs to the linearized zero graph; do not infer the physical nonzero attractor or nonlinear behavior at equality.

value.rationale: The number of quasiperiodic driving coordinates is a built-in structural parameter of the published pinched family. A strict complete dimension staircase is an invariant stability statement, not a cherry-picked special case. Its d=2 threshold has a non-obvious Apéry constant; the second asymptotic coefficient and sharp location of the dimension-induced sign switch quantify the critical regime at every near-limiting coupling. The theorem gives a motivated phase classification without pretending to infer unrelated attractor properties.
